Business_Problem_13.name: Public_Relations_Crisis_Management
Business_Problem_13.background_context: A global consumer brand has recently faced negative public reaction in a specific international market due to an advertising campaign that was intended to be humorous but was interpreted as insensitive and disrespectful based on local cultural values. The brand needs to respond quickly and effectively.
Business_Problem_13.business_problem: Outline a strategy for managing a public relations crisis in an international market caused by a cultural misunderstanding in a marketing campaign and suggest steps to restore the brand's reputation.

Business_Problem_7.name: Negotiation_Strategy
Business_Problem_7.background_context: A company is seeking to form a strategic partnership through a joint venture with a potential partner company located in a different country. Initial interactions suggest that the negotiation process may involve different communication styles and expectations compared to previous experiences.
Business_Problem_7.business_problem: Outline a negotiation strategy for establishing a joint venture with a company from a different country, considering potential differences in communication styles, decision-making processes, and relationship-building approaches.

Business_Problem_6.name: Ethical_Marketing_Campaign
Business_Problem_6.background_context: A company producing health and wellness products is planning a new marketing campaign to promote a recently launched dietary supplement. The campaign needs to be developed for a specific market with unique social values and beliefs related to health, well-being, and advertising.
Business_Problem_6.business_problem: Design an ethical and effective marketing campaign for a health supplement targeting a specific international market, taking into account local social values, beliefs, and advertising norms.

Business_Problem_12.name: Sustainable_Tourism_Development
Business_Problem_12.background_context: A government tourism agency in a region with significant natural beauty and historical sites wants to develop its tourism industry to attract more international visitors. A key goal is to ensure that tourism growth is environmentally sustainable and benefits local communities while preserving cultural heritage.
Business_Problem_12.business_problem: Propose a plan for developing sustainable tourism in a region, focusing on attracting international visitors while protecting the environment, respecting local culture, and providing economic benefits to the community.

Business_Problem_15.name: Future_of_Work
Business_Problem_15.background_context: Following a period of significant change, a large international company is re-evaluating its approach to where and how its employees work, including considerations for remote work, office spaces, and team collaboration tools. The goal is to create a flexible and effective work environment for employees worldwide.
Business_Problem_15.business_problem: Propose a framework or set of principles for designing the "future of work" within a global company, taking into account the varied needs, preferences, and cultural expectations of employees in different countries.

Business_Problem_1.name: Market_Entry_Strategy
Business_Problem_1.background_context: A mid-sized company specializing in environmentally friendly clothing has established a strong presence in Western European markets. They are now looking to expand their business into a new geographical region to access new customer segments and manufacturing opportunities.
Business_Problem_1.business_problem: Propose a comprehensive strategy for entering and establishing a presence in a new international market. Consider product positioning, marketing channels, and initial operational steps.

Business_Problem_14.name: Designing_Inclusive_Products/Services
Business_Problem_14.background_context: A technology company is in the process of designing a new digital product that is intended for a global user base. The company wants to ensure that the product is inclusive and accessible to people from diverse cultural backgrounds and does not inadvertently exclude or offend any user groups.
Business_Problem_14.business_problem: Suggest features, design considerations, and content guidelines for a new digital product to ensure it is inclusive and respectful of diverse cultural backgrounds among its global users.

Business_Problem_3.name: Innovative_Customer_Service
Business_Problem_3.background_context: An online retail company wants to enhance its customer service operations to increase customer satisfaction and loyalty in a specific regional market where recent feedback indicates that current support methods are not fully meeting customer expectations.
Business_Problem_3.business_problem: Suggest innovative approaches and improvements for customer service in a regional market to increase customer satisfaction and build stronger customer relationships.

Business_Problem_2.name: Cross_Cultural_Team_Collaboration
Business_Problem_2.background_context: A multinational technology company operates with project teams whose members are geographically distributed across several continents. These teams are experiencing communication delays and occasional misunderstandings, impacting project timelines and team cohesion.
Business_Problem_2.business_problem: Develop strategies and best practices to improve communication, foster better collaboration, and resolve conflicts effectively within geographically dispersed, culturally diverse project teams.

Business_Problem_9.name: Managing_Innovation
Business_Problem_9.background_context: An established company aims to become more innovative and responsive to market changes. They want to encourage employees across all their international branches to contribute new ideas and experiment with novel approaches, but the level of proactive innovation varies significantly by location.
Business_Problem_9.business_problem: Suggest strategies for fostering a more innovative culture and encouraging employee creativity and risk-taking within an international company with offices in different countries.

Business_Problem_5.name: Adapting_Leadership_Styles
Business_Problem_5.background_context: A large international corporation is rolling out a new global initiative focused on empowering employees and fostering a more adaptable organizational culture. The success of this initiative depends on effective leadership across all regional offices.
Business_Problem_5.business_problem: Provide guidance on how leadership and management approaches can be effectively adapted and applied in different international regions to support a global initiative focused on employee empowerment and cultural change.

Business_Problem_11.name: Adapting_Educational_Technology
Business_Problem_11.background_context: A company provides an online platform and digital content for K-12 education. They are planning to introduce their services into a new country with a different educational system structure, pedagogical traditions, and technological infrastructure compared to their current markets.
Business_Problem_11.business_problem: Suggest ways to adapt an online educational technology platform and its content to be effective and well-received in a new international market with a different educational system and teaching methods.

Business_Problem_10.name: Talent_Management_and_Motivation
Business_Problem_10.background_context: A global company employs a diverse workforce spanning numerous countries and cultural backgrounds. The human resources department is seeking to develop talent management and employee motivation programs that are effective and perceived as fair and engaging by employees in all locations.
Business_Problem_10.business_problem: Design approaches for talent management and employee motivation that can be successfully implemented and resonate with a culturally diverse global workforce.

Business_Problem_4.name: Product_Development_for_a_New_Market
Business_Problem_4.original_title: Product Development for a New Market
Business_Problem_4.background_context: A company that develops and sells snack foods is planning to introduce a new product line specifically tailored for consumers in a target international market with distinct local tastes and eating habits. Market research indicates a demand for new and interesting snack options.
Business_Problem_4.business_problem: Generate ideas for a new snack product line specifically designed for a target international market, considering local taste preferences, ingredients, and consumption occasions.

Business_Problem_8.name: Supply_Chain_Resilience
Business_Problem_8.background_context: A manufacturing company sources raw materials and components from various suppliers located in multiple countries. Recent global events have highlighted the need to enhance the resilience and ethical standards of its supply chain to minimize disruptions and ensure responsible sourcing.
Business_Problem_8.business_problem: Propose strategies and actions to improve the resilience and ethical considerations within a global supply chain that involves sourcing from diverse international locations.

Business_Problem_16.name: Low_Cost_Disruptor_Response
Business_Problem_16.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_16.background_context: A mid-sized appliance manufacturer with a 30-year reputation for durable, premium products is losing market share to a new entrant selling functional, no-frills alternatives at 40% lower prices through online channels only. The incumbent's retail partners are demanding price concessions, while its engineering culture resists anything perceived as lowering quality standards. Margins are still healthy but volume has declined for six consecutive quarters.
Business_Problem_16.business_problem: Develop a strategic response to the low-cost disruptor. Should the company defend the premium position, launch a fighter brand, restructure its cost base, or pursue another path? Propose a coherent strategy with clear reasoning about trade-offs, sequencing, and how to bring retail partners and the internal engineering culture along.

Business_Problem_17.name: Single_Product_Diversification
Business_Problem_17.original_title: Diversification Decision for a Single-Product Company
Business_Problem_17.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_17.background_context: A profitable company earns 95% of its revenue from a single flagship product whose core market is mature and growing at under 2% per year. The board is concerned about concentration risk, but two previous diversification attempts failed because they strayed too far from the company's capabilities. The company has strong cash reserves, a loyal customer base, and deep expertise in its niche.
Business_Problem_17.business_problem: Design a diversification strategy that reduces single-product dependency without repeating past failures. Identify what kinds of adjacencies to pursue, how to evaluate them against the company's actual capabilities, whether to build, buy, or partner, and how to stage investment so early failures do not endanger the core business.

Business_Problem_18.name: Legacy_Brand_Repositioning
Business_Problem_18.original_title: Repositioning a Legacy Brand for Younger Consumers
Business_Problem_18.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_18.background_context: A 70-year-old consumer brand is trusted by older customers but seen as outdated by consumers under 35, whose purchase share is declining every year. Previous 'modernization' campaigns were mocked as inauthentic and briefly alienated the loyal base. The brand retains strong distribution, high awareness, and a genuine heritage story, but internal teams disagree on how much change the brand can absorb.
Business_Problem_18.business_problem: Create a repositioning strategy that makes the brand relevant to younger consumers without losing the existing loyal base. Define the new positioning, which brand elements to preserve versus retire, the channel and content approach, and how to sequence the transition so the brand avoids another authenticity backlash.

Business_Problem_19.name: DTC_Channel_Without_Alienating_Retail
Business_Problem_19.original_title: Building a Direct-to-Consumer Channel Without Alienating Retail Partners
Business_Problem_19.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_19.background_context: A consumer goods company sells almost entirely through third-party retailers, who control shelf placement and customer data. Management wants a direct-to-consumer channel to capture first-party data and higher margins, but its two largest retail partners together account for 55% of revenue and have punished suppliers who competed with them directly. An earlier quiet pilot of a web store triggered an angry call from one partner's buying team.
Business_Problem_19.business_problem: Design a go-to-market plan for building a meaningful direct-to-consumer business while keeping the retail relationships that fund the company today. Specify the channel architecture, product and pricing differentiation between channels, the data strategy, and the partner-communication plan that prevents open channel conflict.

Business_Problem_20.name: Lead_Time_Reduction_Quality
Business_Problem_20.original_title: Reducing Production Lead Times Under Quality Constraints
Business_Problem_20.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_20.background_context: An industrial equipment maker quotes 14-week lead times while its fastest competitor quotes 6, and sales reports losing one in three deals on delivery speed alone. The product requires certified quality inspections at multiple stages, and the last attempt to compress the schedule caused a spike in warranty claims that took two years to live down. Production, quality, and sales each blame the others' processes.
Business_Problem_20.business_problem: Develop an operations improvement plan that substantially reduces quoted lead time without compromising certified quality standards. Identify where time is actually lost, which process, inventory, scheduling, or supplier changes to make, how to protect quality gates, and how to align the three feuding functions around the plan.

Business_Problem_21.name: Warehouse_Automation_Workforce
Business_Problem_21.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_21.background_context: A distribution company operating five regional warehouses faces rising labor costs, 35% annual picker turnover, and error rates that damage key accounts. Automation vendors promise a 3-year payback, but the workforce includes hundreds of long-tenured employees, the largest warehouse is the main employer in its town, and a botched automation rollout at a competitor made national news. Capital is available but not unlimited.
Business_Problem_21.business_problem: Create an automation and workforce-transition roadmap for the warehouse network. Decide the degree and sequence of automation per site, how to redeploy, retrain, or reduce staff responsibly, how to maintain service levels during conversion, and how to measure whether the program is delivering its promised returns.

Business_Problem_22.name: Supplier_Concentration_Risk
Business_Problem_22.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_22.background_context: A machinery producer sources a critical precision component from a single supplier that holds unique tooling and process know-how; qualifying an alternative would take 18 months and significant engineering effort. The supplier has recently been acquired by a competitor's parent company, raised prices twice, and slipped on delivery dates. Redesigning the product to use a different component is possible but would delay the next product generation.
Business_Problem_22.business_problem: Formulate a supply risk strategy for the critical component. Weigh dual-sourcing, strategic inventory, contractual protections, partial vertical integration, and product redesign; recommend a portfolio of actions with timeline and cost logic, and define the triggers that would escalate from mitigation to full independence from the supplier.

Business_Problem_23.name: Reverse_Logistics_Returns
Business_Problem_23.original_title: Profitable Reverse Logistics for Product Returns at Scale
Business_Problem_23.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_23.background_context: An online retailer's return rate has climbed to 28% of shipped units, and processing returns now costs more per unit than the original outbound fulfillment. Returned goods pile up in a manual inspection queue, many are resold too late at deep discounts, and a growing share is simply scrapped. Customer research warns that tightening the return policy is the single fastest way to lose share to rivals.
Business_Problem_23.business_problem: Redesign the returns operation so it stops destroying margin without degrading the customer promise. Address return prevention, triage and grading, refurbishment and secondary channels, network design for reverse flows, and the data feedback loop to merchandising — and quantify how success should be measured.

Business_Problem_24.name: Post_Merger_Workforce_Integration
Business_Problem_24.original_title: Post-Merger Integration of Two Corporate Workforces
Business_Problem_24.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_24.background_context: Two similarly sized companies in the same industry have merged: one is process-driven and hierarchical, the other informal and founder-led. Six months in, duplicate roles remain unresolved, top performers from the acquired firm are being recruited away, and decision-making has slowed because nobody is sure whose processes apply. The deal's synergy case assumed 15% overhead reduction that has not started.
Business_Problem_24.business_problem: Design the people and organization integration plan for the merged company. Decide the target operating model, how to select leaders and resolve duplicate roles fairly, how to retain critical talent, which processes to standardize versus leave alone, and the sequence and communication plan that restores decision speed while delivering the synergy commitments.

Business_Problem_25.name: Subscription_Revenue_Transition
Business_Problem_25.original_title: Transitioning from One-Time Sales to Subscription Revenue
Business_Problem_25.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_25.background_context: A software company sells perpetual licenses with paid upgrades, producing lumpy revenue that investors discount heavily. Leadership wants to move to subscriptions, but modeling shows a multi-year revenue trough during the transition, the sales force is paid on large upfront deals, and long-standing customers feel entitled to the licenses they already bought. A competitor that switched abruptly lost a fifth of its installed base.
Business_Problem_25.business_problem: Plan the business-model transition to subscription revenue. Define the offer structure and migration incentives for existing license holders, the pricing that balances trough depth against adoption, the sales compensation redesign, and the financial communication plan that keeps investors and the board committed through the trough.

Business_Problem_26.name: Pricing_Under_Cost_Inflation
Business_Problem_26.original_title: Pricing Strategy Under Sustained Input-Cost Inflation
Business_Problem_26.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_26.background_context: A packaged-foods producer has absorbed eighteen months of raw material, energy, and freight cost increases that have compressed gross margin by six points. Two blunt price increases were partially rejected: one major grocery chain delisted three products, and volume fell faster than forecast in price-sensitive segments. Competitors are shrinking pack sizes, reformulating, and discounting tactically in ways that muddy price comparisons.
Business_Problem_26.business_problem: Develop a pricing and margin-recovery strategy under sustained cost inflation. Combine list-price moves, pack architecture, mix management, promotion redesign, and targeted cost engineering; specify how to differentiate actions across channels and segments, and how to negotiate the plan with powerful retail customers without further delistings.

Business_Problem_27.name: Scaleup_Growth_Funding_Choice
Business_Problem_27.original_title: Funding Growth: Debt, Equity, or Organic Cash for a Scale-up
Business_Problem_27.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_27.background_context: A profitable scale-up doubling revenue every two years has an opportunity to accelerate: demand exceeds capacity, and a rival is raising heavily to chase the same market. The founders hold 78% equity and prize independence; the company generates cash but not enough to fund the required capacity, hiring, and market expansion simultaneously. Banks offer covenant-heavy debt, growth funds offer capital at a valuation the founders consider low, and going slower risks ceding the market window.
Business_Problem_27.business_problem: Recommend a growth-financing strategy. Compare debt, minority equity, hybrid instruments, and disciplined organic growth against the company's risk tolerance, the competitive window, and the founders' control preferences; propose a funding structure, the milestones it should be staged against, and the walk-away conditions for each source.

Business_Problem_28.name: Loss_Making_Unit_Turnaround
Business_Problem_28.original_title: Turning Around a Loss-Making Business Unit
Business_Problem_28.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_28.background_context: A diversified group's industrial-services unit has lost money for three straight years despite two restructuring attempts that cut costs but not losses. The unit serves some customers who also buy from the group's profitable divisions, its order book is shrinking, and its best managers keep transferring out. The board has given leadership one final year to produce a credible path to profitability or exit.
Business_Problem_28.business_problem: Produce the turnaround-or-exit assessment and plan. Diagnose whether the losses are structural or execution-driven, identify which customer segments and service lines could sustain profit, design the turnaround plan with milestones for the one-year deadline, and define the exit alternatives and the criteria for choosing between turnaround and divestment.

Business_Problem_29.name: Monetizing_Free_User_Base
Business_Problem_29.original_title: Monetizing a Large Free User Base Without Driving Churn
Business_Problem_29.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_29.background_context: A consumer app has grown to millions of active free users but converts under 2% to its paid tier, and investor patience with the losses is ending. Past monetization tests backfired: aggressive paywalls spiked uninstalls, and intrusive ads damaged app-store ratings within weeks. Usage data shows several distinct user segments that get very different value from the product.
Business_Problem_29.business_problem: Design a monetization strategy that meaningfully increases revenue per user while protecting retention and ratings. Choose and justify the mix of subscription tiers, usage-based pricing, advertising, and partnerships; map offers to the identified user segments; and define the experiment plan and guardrail metrics that will catch churn damage before it compounds.

Business_Problem_30.name: Legacy_Product_Sunset_Migration
Business_Problem_30.original_title: Sunsetting a Legacy Product While Migrating Customers
Business_Problem_30.provenance: Author-drafted domain-stratified extension set (Entry 4); culture-agnostic general business problem
Business_Problem_30.background_context: A technology company still earns a third of its profit from a legacy product it stopped actively developing years ago; the replacement product is stronger but lacks a few niche features that the most loyal legacy customers depend on. Maintenance costs and security exposure on the old platform grow every year, and the engineers who understand it are approaching retirement. Some large customers threaten to switch vendors entirely if forced to migrate.
Business_Problem_30.business_problem: Plan the end-of-life and migration program for the legacy product. Set the sunset timeline and support policy, decide which niche capabilities must be rebuilt versus retired, design migration incentives and tooling for each customer tier, and prepare the retention plan for the customers most likely to defect during the transition.
